decisions.reason: Because the firm publicly launched it on its own page, has already invested in sampling and stocking, and the weak visibility after 2019 can still be explained as normal collection integration in a growing market, management would tend to persist with this close-to-core fabric line.

As a decorative fabric close to the existing assortment, it likely required manageable incremental investment and its disappointing website trail can be justified as temporary or due to catalog reshuffling, which supports continued commitment.

Management would likely continue this burnout decorative fabric because it fits the announced design-led collection strategy, the launch was publicly visible, and there is no clear evidence of failure strong enough to overcome sunk-cost and justification pressures.

This upholstery fabric builds directly on the firm’s established offer and service strengths, so after investing in launch and presentation the firm would be inclined to keep backing it rather than admit the introduction was unsuccessful.

The flame-retardant inbetween fabric extends the range in a functionally attractive way for professional buyers, and management can readily argue that demand may need more time, reinforcing escalation of commitment.

Since this lining fabric is adjacent to the core textile business and likely easy to support through the firm’s stocked warehouse and reorder system, management would tend to retain it despite limited later visibility.
